html:
SMTO-SKL-0009 — Two Skills have the same name, so SMTO needs the exact one

GUID: 516c650a-64f6-4a18-bdc3-4e142d7142f1
Slug: ambiguous-skill
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: skl

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to use a Skill by a name that more than one Skill shares. It didn't pick one by guessing, and nothing was run with either Skill.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Give SMTO a moment. It may pick the right Skill by itself, because the message lists the Skills that share the name. SMTO received the exact names of the matching Skills, so it can often choose correctly without your help.
  2. If it stops, open Settings, expand Details and tools, and select Skills. Each tool listed starts with its Skill's exact name, such as slack in slack.history. That exact name is unique even when two Skills look alike.
  3. Ask again in a new message, naming the Skill by that exact name. An exact name lets SMTO pick the one Skill you meant.

What success looks like

  • SMTO uses the Skill you named and carries on with your request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. If a saved Task or Schedule uses this Skill, don't switch it to a different Skill without checking that it does the same job.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Tool discovery was given a Skill display name that case-insensitively matches more than one registered Skill, so it returned the matching Skill IDs instead of choosing one.

What this means

  • Skill discovery resolves a display name to more than one matching Skill instead of one canonical identity. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Skill discovery resolves a display name to more than one matching Skill instead of one canonical identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect returned candidates and canonical Skill IDs.

How to fix it

  • discover_tools (ToolCatalog._discover in src/agent_runtime/native/catalog.py) resolved the display name to several skill_ids and returned them as matching_skill_ids with error_kind ambiguous_skill. Repeat discovery with one exact skill_id from that list rather than the display name or list order; check the registry for duplicate display names if this recurs.
  • Select one of the returned canonical Skill IDs before discovering or invoking its tools.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One explicit available Skill ID is selected without relying on list order.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
